title: Canary forensics and benchmark log — perf alert investigation
content:
Summary:

On 2024-11-06 at ~02:14 UTC the Canary job for model-gamma-1 triggered a p95 latency alert (threshold 450ms) on the us-west-2 canary cluster. The alert persisted for ~18 minutes and coincided with a small traffic-increase during a routine canary rollout. This doc is the running investigation log: observations, reproducibility attempts, profiling artifacts, candidate root causes, and the bisect/rollback plan.

What we observed (initial):
- Canary p50/p95/p99 jumped: 120ms -> 210ms (p50), 290ms -> 560ms (p95), 420ms -> 980ms (p99).
- Error budget no spike: 5xx stayed flat.
- Throughput steady (QPS +/- 3%).
- Memory (GPU) usage unchanged, CPU user time on host nodes rose by ~12%.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped from 86% -> 63% for the canary group.
- Canary had an image tag with commit sha: 3f7a2b1 (rolling out at 01:58 UTC).

Immediate hypothesis (ordered):
1) rollout introduced a microchange that increases compute per token (e.g., changed attention config, extra layer norm op, disabled kv-caching for some code-path).
2) host-level kernel/runtime change (libtorch/cuBLAS/cuDNN) on the image caused slower matmul kernels for certain tensor shapes.
3) traffic pattern changed — more long-sequence requests causing kv-cache miss amplification.
4) scheduler/placement change causing contention between GPUs and sidecars (less likely given throughput steady).

Data collection steps taken (log):
- Pulled canary and baseline traces: trace IDs recorded in S3 artifact above. Grabbed 10 full request traces at p50/p95/p99 windows.
- Collected flamegraphs from the runtime CPU profiler for canary and baseline (same time window).
- Captured per-request token breakdown: tokenization, embedding lookup, forward pass, kv-cache lookup, post-processing. See sample CSV in S3.
- Exported Prometheus query snapshots for the timestamp range (02:00-02:30 UTC).
- Verified container image differences (diff between 3f7a2b1 and previous 2e1c9f0).

Key findings from traces/profiles:
- Flamegraphs show a ~2.6x increase in time spent inside the attention kernel path for sequence lengths >1024 on canary traces.
- KV-cache miss handling shows a small regression: additional synchronization barrier introduced in commit 3f7a2b1 (see code comment in PR #987).
- Matmul kernel selection shows fallback to a different cuBLAS algo for particular shapes; baseline used algo X, canary used algo Y (slower).
- No increase in GC or Python-level overhead; C++ runtime dominates time delta.

PromQL/dashboard queries used (examples):
- avg_over_time(request_latency_ms{env="canary",model="gamma-1"}[5m])
- histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le))
- sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_requests_total[5m]))
- topk(5, sum(rate(runtime_cpu_seconds_total[5m])) by (kernel))

Repro reproducibility attempts:
- Synthetic replay of the canary workload (same seq-length distribution) against baseline image and canary image on staging GPUs: reproduced 2.3x p95 delta.
- Isolated kernel benchmarking: ran microbench matmul shapes observed — reproduced switch to slower algo when using library versions included in canary image.
- Reproduction fails when we pin older cuBLAS in canary image -> points to library change.

Short-term mitigation considered:
- Rollback the canary image to 2e1c9f0 (fastest, minimal blast radius) — decision: rolled back at 03:12 UTC; canary p95 returned to baseline within one minute.
- Alternative: pin specific kernel selection environment variable (if available) or force different cuBLAS algos via env flags.

Bisect / root cause plan (next steps):
1) Narrow range: commits between 2e1c9f0..3f7a2b1. Focus on changes touching runtime kernel selection, third-party dependency updates, and KV cache sync points.
2) Build images with incremental dependency pins: (a) only change code diffs but keep libraries pinned; (b) change libraries only; (c) combined. Run synthetic benchmark harness for each.
3) If library change reproduces the regression, pin the library in the release branch and open revert PR for the library bump.
4) If code change reproduces it, identify exact function and patch (reintroduce non-blocking path or avoid extra barrier).

Experiment matrix (record results here):
- Exp A: image with code diffs only (libraries pinned) -> result: no regression (PASS)
- Exp B: image with libraries bumped but old runtime code -> result: regression reproduced (FAIL)
- Exp C: image with both -> result: FAIL (same as B)
- Conclusion: library bump appears causal (cuBLAS/cuDNN combo).

Observability follow-ups and dashboard changes: 
- Add a canary-specific kernel-metrics panel: kernel selection distribution (algo id), time-per-kernel heatmap by seq-length.
- Add KV-cache miss-rate alert with separate threshold for canary groups; correlate with p95.
- Capture and store one canonical trace per alert (auto-upload to S3) and link in alert body.

Action items (owners + ETA):
- Aisha: create revert PR for library bump on release branch and coordinate with infra to pin images for next canary rollout. ETA 2024-11-08.
- Markus: run extended microbench suite across all GPU shapes in infra matrix and add results to /benchmarks/kernel-selection/2024-11. ETA 2024-11-09.
- Sofia: extend canary dashboard with kernel-selection panel and KV miss alert rule. ETA 2024-11-10.
- Leah: update incident postmortem template with steps we used here and attach sample flamegraphs. ETA 2024-11-11.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Why did the library bump select a different algo only for the particular tensor shapes? (likely heuristic change in cuBLAS; follow-up with vendor/driver notes).
- Can we add deterministic kernel-selection in our binary to avoid vendor heuristics? Risk/effort analysis needed.
- Are there any other models affected by same lib bump but not caught by canary? Run full-model smoke job across prod-like fleet.

Communication notes (what to tell stakeholders):
- Short: We observed a canary latency regression caused by vendor library changes included in the new image. We rolled back the canary image within an hour; no customer-visible impact. Remediation: pin the library bump and run expanded kernel benchmarks before next rollout.
- Long (postmortem): timeline, root cause analysis, experiment artifacts, improvements to auto-collection and dashboarding, and the rollback decision rationale.

Attachments / artifacts index (S3 + links):
- trace-logs.tar.gz -> s3://redwood-logs/canary/2024-11-06/trace-logs.tar.gz
- flamegraphs/ -> s3://redwood-logs/canary/2024-11-06/flamegraphs/
- microbench-results.csv -> s3://redwood-logs/benchmarks/kernel-selection/2024-11/microbench-results.csv
- PR #987 (runtime change) -> github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/987

Notes-to-self / rough ideas for longer-term:
- Add a deterministic kernel advisory layer in our runtime that selects algo sets (fast/compatible) per model family and seq-length bucket. Start with an opt-in flag.
- Automate bisect: given an alert, spawn test jobs that iterate through candidate images with a synthetic workload and produce a pass/fail matrix.
- Add perf unit tests to CI that run critical matmul shapes and assert p95 within tolerance.

Appendix: quick checklist for next triage run (copyable into alert runbook):
1) Grab alert window timestamps and immediate Prometheus snapshots.
2) Check image tag + git-diff.
3) Pull 3 representative traces (p50, p95, p99) and upload to S3.
4) Run 10 synthetic replay requests against canary image on staging.
5) Run microbench matmul shapes from sample list.
6) If repro, either rollback canary or pin libs and re-run.

End of running log.

(If this doc becomes final postmortem, move to confluence page in linked_artifacts and set status->final.)
